raw.assessment: The incumbent reliably delivered the ordered designs in the previous batch, while its reference-table check caught seven fit problems before dispatch. Rework clustered in large covers (5/8), versus medium (2/14) and small (0/18), supporting investigation of size-dependent dimensional error without establishing its cause. Small unadjusted covers demonstrate feasible individual times below 32 minutes, but do not establish the incoming batch median. A concrete limit is the two observed customer failures on rounded tables: reference-table success may miss customer geometry. Length shrinkage is observed; its contribution to fitting failures and width behavior remain unknown. Estimated waste by weight does not establish the area constraint.

openings.claim: The common allowance may produce a size-dependent dimensional mismatch that contributes to larger-cover rework.
openings.delta: Distinguish an unsuitable cutting target from cutting or sewing variation before applying revised allowances across the stock.
openings.prediction: If the allowance is responsible, accurately cut and sewn panels will still show consistent size-dependent fit residuals on reference tables; irregular residuals associated with operator or cutting direction would weaken this account.
openings.probe: Sequence initial small, medium and large orders through fitting before cutting the remainder. Record card targets, actual cut and finished dimensions, design, direction, operator, adjustment and total working time. Check retained offcuts in both directions through the stipulated wash test. Evaluate any allowance change against planned and actual cutting waste by area.
assumptions: Initial covers remain deliverable in their ordered sizes and designs.
Measurement and sequencing fit the three-week window and 350-unit budget.
Allowance changes require evidence; wash durability must still pass.

openings.claim: Do nominal dimensions and unrepresented corner geometry independently explain customer fit failures after reference-table acceptance?
openings.delta: Test transfer from reference tables to customers' actual tables, separately from production dimensional error.
openings.prediction: A geometry mismatch would produce local corner interference despite matching overall dimensions; a nominal-dimension mismatch would appear in measured length or width.
openings.probe: Use the six willing customers to obtain actual dimensions and corner profiles, prioritizing the four nominal-only orders where possible. Compare with reference geometry and observe first placement on represented customer tables without coaching adjustment.
assumptions: Customers include relevant incoming orders or comparable tables.
Measurements arrive before their panels are cut.
Any subsequent adaptation preserves ordered design, removability, wash performance and cutting limits.

raw.assessment: Size-associated rework and two rounded-corner installation failures suggest two potentially interacting fit problems; neither their causes nor a combined remedy are established. One opening is justified. The previous waste estimate and missing width-shrinkage data cannot establish compliance for a revised pattern.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: combine actual-table geometry records with staged, size-specific allowance calibration at the interface where an order becomes a cutting card. Geometry records supply measured dimensions and corner contours; staged sewing supplies a tested allowance for the relevant size. Together they could produce a first-placement fit that either accurate measurements with an unsuitable allowance, or calibrated allowances applied to an inaccurate table description, would miss.
openings.delta: Replace the common-allowance, whole-batch cutting decision with a geometry-linked cutting card and a first-cover feedback step before cutting further covers in that size/geometry group. Keep every ordered size and printed design.
openings.prediction: On measured tables differing from the reference geometry, the combined card should reduce corner mismatch and seam reopening beyond either change alone. A positive interaction would mean geometry correction improves fit more with the calibrated allowance than with the common allowance. No such difference would weaken the combination hypothesis.
openings.probe: Use measurements from the six willing customers and retained offcuts for matched corner mockups crossing reference versus measured geometry with common versus calibrated allowances. Record mismatch, seating attempts, and sewing time; mockups only screen the interaction. Then stage actual covers, checking specified-table first placement and ordered design, while recording all cooperative labor. Verify five-cycle durability and tool-free removal, cost at most 350, and three-week completion. Calculate cutting waste by area before releasing each cutting layout, capped at 8%. Across all 40 covers require at least 38 first-placement fits and median work at most 32 minutes; unresolved customer geometry prevents claiming that result.
assumptions: Measured geometry transfers adequately into a usable corner pattern.
Allowance calibration remains applicable across the purchased stock despite unmeasured width shrinkage.
Measurement, mockup, and calibration work can fit the budget and schedule, with enough avoided rework to meet the labor target.
The six customer measurements provide useful cases; they are not assumed to resolve all four nominal-only orders.

openings.claim: Common allowance may cause size-dependent mismatch.
openings.discriminator: Consistent residuals despite accurate production support allowance error; operator/direction variation weakens it.
openings.probe: Stage small/medium/large covers before remaining cuts; log target, cut and finished dimensions, design, direction, operator, adjustments and labor. Wash offcuts in both directions.
openings.uncertainty: Cause, width shrinkage and calibration transfer unknown.

openings.claim: Customer dimensions and corner geometry may independently defeat reference-table acceptance.
openings.discriminator: Local corner interference versus overall length/width mismatch.
openings.probe: Obtain dimensions and corner profiles from six customers before cutting; prioritize four nominal-only orders where possible. Compare reference geometry and observe uncoached first placement.
openings.uncertainty: Customer coverage and timely measurements unconfirmed.

openings.claim: Geometry-linked cards plus staged allowance calibration may interact to improve fit.
openings.discriminator: Geometry correction improves fit more with calibrated than common allowances.
openings.probe: Cross reference/measured geometry with common/calibrated allowances in matched offcut mockups; record mismatch, seating attempts and time, then stage actual covers.
openings.uncertainty: Mockups only screen interaction; pattern transfer and labor savings unproven.

post_distill.decision: Probe before releasing remaining cuts. Preserve ordered sizes/designs and purchased stock; verify five-cycle durability, tool-free removal, existing two machines, cost <=350 and completion within three weeks. Measure waste by area <=8%; prior weight estimate is insufficient. Count all cooperative labor: require >=38/40 specified-table first-placement fits, every ordered design and median <=32 minutes. Unresolved geometry prevents claiming success.
